summary_paragraph: A woman with metastatic breast cancer and refractory gastroparesis was admitted due to a clogged G-tube that ruptured, causing leakage of contents and a chemical skin rash. She developed worsening nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. A new 16 French GJ tube was placed, but it clogged again, requiring replacement with an 18 French tube. During admission, she was diagnosed with recurrent C. difficile infection, treated with oral vancomycin. Skin irritation around the tube site was managed with mupirocin and betamethasone cream. Tube feeds were resumed with Osmolite 1.5, which she tolerated well. She improved clinically, with resolution of symptoms and stable vitals, and was discharged home with services to complete her vancomycin course and continue home care.
